title: Anxiety and the Peace of Christ
subtitle: A guided route through the worry that will not turn off — four essays, a study, and a book.
forWhom: For the reader who lies awake running the same loop, and who knows the difference between the fear a doctor should hear and the fear only the Father can quiet.

movements.heading: Read these first
movements.note: Begin under the worry, not on top of it. These four move from what Jesus actually said to why fear is so good at rewriting your picture of God.

items.label: What Jesus Said About Worry and Money
items.blurb: The birds and the lilies were never a greeting card. They are an argument about what holds you.

items.label: When Fear Starts Rewriting What You Believe
items.blurb: Anxiety does not only make you afraid. It quietly edits your picture of God.

items.label: The Restless Man Who Couldn't Outrun God
items.blurb: Augustine named the ache sixteen centuries early: the heart is restless until it rests in God.

items.label: Why a Day of Doing Nothing Is an Act of Defiance
items.blurb: Stopping for a full day — no work, no producing, no proving — feels almost impossible to a culture organized around output.

movements.heading: Then work the study
movements.note: Consider the Birds is a five-session guide — honest about the anxiety that needs a doctor, pastoral about the anxiety that needs the Father. Run it alone or with a group.

items.label: Consider the Birds — a study on anxiety
items.blurb: Five sessions, with the answer behind every question already written for the leader.
